title: DuckDuckGo pitches itself to schools amid backlash over Google’s AI policy
slides: Why are schools rethinking Google right now?
DuckDuckGo is pitching itself as the alternative.
Its pitch leans on privacy, not better search results.
Schools switching face real migration friction and costs.
Ask your school which search tool it actually trusts.
thread_text:
1. The quiet search shift

Schools are moving away from Google as their default search tool — not because of features, but because of a privacy roadmap nobody asked for.

2. DuckDuckGo's angle

The company isn't trying to out-Google Google on results. It's selling one thing: a search box that doesn't build a profile of every student.

3. Privacy isn't a feature

For IT admins, 'we don't track you' is the whole pitch. That reframes procurement from speed and relevance to data governance and liability.

4. The cost of leaving

Switching isn't just a toggle. Schools face single sign-on breakage, extension rebuilds, staff retraining, and real budget line items for migration.

5. Ask the hard question

Ask your school which search tool it actually trusts — and whether the privacy claim is verified or just marketing. Then check the contract.
